sites.name_ar: المسجد الأقصى المبارك / الحرم القدسي الشريف

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Al-Aqsa Mosque/Al-Haram Al-Sharif is addressed by UNESCO as a Muslim holy site of worship and an integral part of the Old City of Jerusalem World Heritage property.

held_claims.claim_text: claims about a Canaanite temple, exact location of ancient temples, absence/presence of archaeological evidence under the compound, and effects of excavations on foundations
held_claims.reason: Not established by the official sources inspected in this wave.

coordinate_review.note: UNESCO coordinate for Old City of Jerusalem is property-wide and must not be assigned to Al-Aqsa as a site coordinate.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Silwan is part of the geo-historic context immediately outside the Old City; the Gihon Spring is identified in a State Party submission as a focal water source in Jerusalem's development.
UNESCO monitoring documents record reports and concerns concerning excavation and tunnelling activities in Silwan.

held_claims.claim_text: Canaanite/Roman/Islamic period sequence for the whole town
Specific excavation impacts and current physical condition

corrections: Do not treat the tentative-list submission as a settled neutral archaeological synthesis.
Claims of specific damage or removed strata must be attributed to the reporting party and separately corroborated.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The Western/Wailing Wall is identified by UNESCO as one of the major monuments of the Old City property.
A 1930 international commission was established to determine Muslim and Jewish rights and claims connected with the Wall.

corrections: Do not infer the current legal status solely from the 1930 commission without contemporary legal review.
Hold precise Herodian construction attribution and 1967 surrounding-area demolition claims until dedicated archaeological and archival sources are linked.
No dedicated authoritative or academic record sufficiently identifying Khan al-Jawabra was located in this wave.
Keep catalog identity only; do not publish the Ottoman attribution.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Suq al-Qattanin is a Mamluk market terminating at Tariq al-Wad and connecting through Bab al-Qattanin to the Haram al-Sharif precinct.

held_claims.claim_text: Exact patron and construction date pending direct bibliography inspection

corrections: Use a fourteenth-century Mamluk context; publication-level construction dates must cite the architectural bibliography directly.
Do not infer the detailed cotton trade economy from the place-name alone.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The Greek Orthodox Patriarchate maintains the living tradition identifying the Gethsemane shrine as the Tomb of the Virgin Mary.
The Studium Biblicum Franciscanum records archaeological excavation work at Gethsemane and the Tomb of Mary.

corrections: Burial attribution must remain RELIGIOUS_TRADITION.
Byzantine and Crusader phase dates require the excavation publications, not only institutional overview pages.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Al-Wad Street contains major Mamluk architectural institutions and connects with the Qattanin market/gate complex.

held_claims.claim_text: Individual dates, patrons, coordinates, and rights

corrections: The catalog label groups multiple palaces, madrasas, ribats, and other institutions and must not be treated as a single monument.
Create a constituent inventory before publication or mapping.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The present citadel is a multi-period composition incorporating Roman fortification and Crusader, Ayyubid, Mamluk, and Ottoman construction.

held_claims.claim_text: Exact attribution of each tower and phase

corrections: The name 'Tower of David' must be stored as a historical/popular name with usage context, not as proof of association with David.
The catalog period list should distinguish surviving fabric from earlier remains.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The Church of the Holy Sepulchre is a major monument within the Old City World Heritage property; UNESCO identifies the Resurrection rotunda as housing Christ's tomb within Christian tradition.
The Studium Biblicum Franciscanum records archaeological excavation work at the Holy Sepulchre.

corrections: The tomb identification remains a Christian tradition; archaeological phases require direct excavation publications.
Do not use simplified single-date construction narratives.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: A UNESCO monitoring document records the Jordanian and Palestinian report describing Nabi Dawoud Mosque as an Islamic Waqf property next to the southern wall of the Old City and reporting alterations there.
Mount Zion forms part of the wider geo-historic and religious context described in a postponed State Party extension proposal.

corrections: Do not present the burial attribution to Prophet David as historically or archaeologically verified.
The catalog's Umayyad/Mamluk/Ottoman sequence remains unverified in this wave.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The monumental enclosure around the sacred cave was constructed in the 1st century AD.
The site is associated with traditions concerning Abraham/Ibrahim and is venerated by three monotheistic religions.

held_claims.claim_text: claim_group=claims of exclusive religious ownership, detailed modern access restrictions, the 1994 massacre and post-1994 partition arrangements | status=HOLD_FOR_DEDICATED_LEGAL_AND_CONTEMPORARY_SOURCE_WAVE

coordinate_review.note: The UNESCO coordinate is for the old-town property, not an exact coordinate for the mosque compound.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The old town substantially preserves Mamluk urban morphology with later Ottoman additions.
The Al-Ibrahimi Mosque/Tomb of Patriarchs monumental compound is central to the old town and the enclosure dates to the 1st century AD.
The place is venerated by Judaism, Christianity and Islam.

corrections: No sufficiently specific authoritative record for the combined identity 'Beit Ummar / Khirbet Nabi Matta' was inspected.
Separate locality identity from shrine/ruin identity before research.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Tell Rumeida is included in the archaeological remains of the buffer-zone context of Hebron/Al-Khalil Old Town.
ICOMOS documented that Tell Rumeida was excluded from the original nominated property boundary and discussed evidence of earlier settlement in its vicinity.

corrections: Do not equate buffer-zone inclusion with a complete archaeological validation of every Bronze/Canaanite/Roman claim.
Detailed layer chronology requires excavation reports.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The Nabi Yunus mosque/maqam is in old Halhul; the monument record dates it to AH 623 / AD 1226, identifies an Ayyubid patron, and records later Mamluk renovation.

corrections: The tomb's attribution to Prophet Jonah must remain RELIGIOUS_TRADITION.
The catalog's Canaanite and Ottoman period labels require independent sources.
UNESCO confirms khans as a building category in Hebron Old Town but does not specifically identify Khan al-Hatab.
Keep Ottoman attribution and component identity blocked.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: WAFA documents the existence of Nabi Nuh shrine in Dura as a local religious and historical landmark and records community restoration and charitable use by 2020.

corrections: Do not infer Mamluk or Ottoman construction dates from this source.
The attribution to Prophet Noah remains local religious tradition.
No directly inspected authoritative source sufficiently supports the Roman/Islamic period labels for Ain Sara in this wave.
No sufficiently specific authoritative record was located for the combined identity 'Carmel Castle / Deir Samet'.
Identity may conflate separate sites and requires cadastral/toponymic review.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: UNESCO identifies the sacred Cave of Machpelah/al-Ghar al-Sharif inside the monumental Al-Ibrahimi Mosque/Tomb of Patriarchs complex and treats its burial associations as tradition.

corrections: This record is a component of the already reviewed Ibrahimi complex, not an independently validated public site.
Create a parent-child component relation and prevent duplicate map/publication records.
The catalog's standalone Canaanite period label is not supported by the inspected source.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: ICOMOS specifically discusses the Sheikh Ali al-Bakka area as an excluded area relevant to the integrity and earlier street patterns of Hebron Old Town.

corrections: This does not verify the individual maqam's date, architecture, or saintly biography.
A dedicated architectural or waqf source is still required.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The conservation project documents three historic pools and an Ottoman Murad castle; the project was completed in 2012 using distinguishable and reversible interventions.

corrections: The inspected source does not prove Roman construction, the complete Byzantine/Umayyad sequence, or attribution of restoration to Sultan Suleiman.
The canonical coordinate remains available for review only and was not independently surveyed in this wave.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The Greek Orthodox Patriarchate officially lists a Monastery of St George in Al-Khader.

held_claims.claim_text: Synonymy of Deir al-Jannah and St George monastery

corrections: The catalog title 'Deir al-Jannah' was not confirmed as the same official monument name.
Do not retain Byzantine/Crusader period labels until identity and chronology are reconciled.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The Patriarchate's institutional history places the formation of Saint Savvas' Lavra around AD 483 and describes long continuous monastic activity.

corrections: A phase-by-phase architectural narrative requires archaeological publications.
Avoid unqualified global superlatives such as 'one of the oldest continuously inhabited monasteries' unless a comparative source defines the claim.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Battir is a Palestinian cultural landscape of dry-stone terraces and a complex irrigation system supporting olives and vegetables.
The family water-distribution system uses a time-managed rotation and mathematical allocation.

corrections: draft_pattern=irrigation has operated for thousands of years | disposition=QUALIFY | replacement=UNESCO says terraces may have been exploited since antiquity and describes continuity for at least a millennium; avoid a stronger duration without another source.

coordinate_review.note: The property has two components; preserve as component coordinates or polygon data.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: A substantial published excavation corpus exists for Herodium, including Corbo's palace-fortress report and later final reports for the 1972–2010 excavations.
Published academic chapters address Byzantine churches and inscriptions at Herodion.

corrections: The corpus must be inspected volume-by-volume before publishing claims about Herod's tomb, construction phases, revolts, or later occupation.
Research-corpus confirmation is not equivalent to site-claim verification.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The conservation record identifies an Ottoman Murad castle as part of the Solomon's Pools historical-site complex.

corrections: Treat Castle of the Pools as a component of the Solomon's Pools complex unless an independent boundary and identity are established.
Do not create duplicate public map markers without a parent-child component model.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The location has been identified by Christian tradition as the birthplace of Jesus since the 2nd century.
A church was first completed there in AD 339; the replacement building after a 6th-century fire retains mosaics from the original.

corrections: draft_pattern=built in 326 by Helena | disposition=REPLACE_OR_QUALIFY | replacement=UNESCO states that a church was completed in AD 339; attribution to Helena requires a separate directly inspected source.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The Milk Grotto is a local sanctuary near the Nativity Basilica with a living devotion shared by Christian and Muslim women.
The SBF records an emergency excavation at the sanctuary in October 2005.

corrections: The Holy Family and milk-drop narrative must remain RELIGIOUS_TRADITION.
The canonical Byzantine period label requires direct archaeological publication support.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Birzeit contains a governed historic centre whose buildings, public spaces, infrastructure, and boundaries were documented and rehabilitated through a long-term Riwaq programme.
The Palestinian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities provides contextual reference to a fortified castle in Birzeit.

held_claims.claim_text: Exact castle identity, date, and surviving fabric

corrections: Represent Old Birzeit as a historic urban cluster, not a single generic town point.
The Ottoman-only period classification is too narrow and should remain draft pending architectural inventory.
The castle must become a candidate constituent record only after a dedicated source and boundary are found.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Aboud is recognized within Riwaq's historic-centres programme.
The Aboud landscape includes a sixth-century St Barbara church ruin, a Roman-road and cemetery context, and a separately documented multi-phase Dormition church.

held_claims.claim_text: Current condition and rights for each component

corrections: The title 'Khirbet Aboud' collapses a living historic centre and multiple distinct churches, cemeteries, presses, caves, and ruins.
Split the record into a governed Aboud historic-centre cluster and separate constituent sites.
Do not assign one Roman/Byzantine chronology to the entire undifferentiated record.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Riwaq recognizes Deir Ammar as a Palestinian historic-centre record.

corrections: The canonical type 'monastery/ruin' does not match the confirmed living historic-centre identity.
Roman and Byzantine period labels remain unsupported by the inspected source.
Reclassify as a historic town/village cluster pending detailed survey.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Academic records document Intermediate/Middle Bronze Age shaft-tomb and assemblage evidence at Ain Samiya.
The official Palestinian route guide distinguishes Ain Samiya, Khirbet Marjameh, a palace feature, and Khirbet Samiya within the wider landscape.

held_claims.claim_text: Exact relation between cemetery and nearby settlement

corrections: The canonical record conflates the spring, cemetery, Khirbet Marjameh, Khirbet Samiya, and other features.
Create separate hydrological, archaeological-cemetery, settlement/ruin, and architectural candidate records.
The generic 'Canaanite/Roman' period pair is not an adequate or verified summary.
No authoritative Palestinian heritage, conservation, archival, or academic record for a historic 'Qasr al-Rayan' in Ramallah was located.
Search results were dominated by unrelated contemporary event-hall usage.
Do not substitute Alhambra Palace or another Ramallah building without explicit evidence.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Riwaq records conservation and adaptive reuse of the An Nabi Salih Cultural Center complex completed in 2003 with a local partner.

corrections: The Ayyubid period label is not supported by the inspected Riwaq record.
The tomb attribution to Prophet Salih remains religious and local tradition.
A component inventory is needed to distinguish prayer hall, tomb room, courtyard, press, well, and later cultural-centre functions.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Old Nablus is a historic urban cluster with Roman, Islamic, medieval, Ottoman, religious, commercial, residential, and water-related components.
UNESCO and partners completed restoration and adaptive reuse of Khan al-Wakala as a component of Old Nablus.

corrections: Treat Old Nablus as a governed urban cluster, not a single-point monument.
Create constituent relations for mosques, markets, baths, quarters, khans, and archaeological components.
Tentative-list narratives remain attributed State Party material.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Al-Nasr Mosque is an identified spatial component bordering Bab al-Saha and Al-Nasr Street within Old Nablus.

corrections: The inspected source is contextual, not a dedicated architectural record.
Do not retain Ayyubid and Mamluk period labels as verified.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Mount Gerizim is the living sacred centre of the Samaritan community and contains major Hellenistic, Roman, Byzantine, and Islamic remains.

corrections: Samaritan claims about Abraham, Isaac, Joshua, and temple primacy remain RELIGIOUS_TRADITION.
The UNESCO coordinate is an external State Party reference point and is not promoted.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Al-Yasmina is one of the recognized quarters of Old Nablus; Hosh al-Atout preserves Ottoman residential courtyard fabric.
The official portal reports severe damage in 2002 and reconstruction completed in 2012 for Hosh al-Atout.

corrections: A single courtyard does not verify the entire quarter.
A constituent-building and rights inventory is required.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Khan al-Tujjar is a recognized historic market/fabric-market component of Old Nablus.

corrections: Do not conflate Khan al-Tujjar with Khan al-Wakala.
The Ottoman-only period label requires direct architectural evidence.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The State of Palestine submitted Sebastia to UNESCO's Tentative List in 2012.
The submission describes it as the Iron Age II capital and a major Hellenistic/Roman urban centre, and records major excavation campaigns.
Christian and Islamic traditions associate the site with John the Baptist/Yahya.

corrections: The canonical locality says 'near Nablus (Sinjil)', but Sinjil belongs to Ramallah and al-Bireh Governorate.
The record may conflate different Nabi Shuayb shrines.
Block publication, coordinates, and Mamluk/Ottoman period labels pending identity reconciliation.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Maqam Yusuf near Balata has been revered in Muslim, Christian, Jewish, and Samaritan traditions and has had changing Palestinian social and religious meanings.
The inspected academic article states that archaeological evidence does not verify competing burial identifications.

corrections: Burial attribution to Prophet Joseph remains disputed religious tradition.
Fatimid and Mamluk period labels require dedicated architectural or archaeological sources.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Al-Sibat market is a late Ottoman component within Jenin's older neighbourhoods and is reported above Roman and Byzantine archaeological context.
Fatima Khatun Mosque is a major sixteenth-century Ottoman urban component in central Jenin.

corrections: Treat Old Jenin as an urban cluster requiring a boundary and constituent inventory.
The canonical Mamluk/Ottoman summary is too coarse for publication.
The Ministry portal references Tell Jenin only comparatively in records for other tells and does not provide a dedicated record.
Do not confuse Tell Jenin with Tell al-Hafira, Tell Ti'inik, or Tell al-Mutasallim.
Block Bronze/Canaanite labels until a site-specific excavation record is found.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The official Palestinian heritage portal locates Al-Kayed Palace in Sebastia, Nablus Governorate, and dates construction to 1858.

held_claims.claim_text: Whether a separate Jenin palace with the same name exists

corrections: The canonical Jenin assignment conflicts with the official location in Sebastia.
Do not publish this as a Jenin site.
Perform duplicate/relationship review against the already verified Sebastia cluster.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Burqin Church is a living Greek Orthodox church in Burqin with an official Byzantine heritage attribution.

corrections: The Ten Lepers narrative remains Christian tradition.
Block global rankings such as third, fourth, or fifth oldest church.
Direct excavation publications are required for phase chronology.
No site-specific authoritative or academic source for Maqam Sheikh Hassan in Jenin was located.
Block the Mamluk period label, coordinates, saint biography, and publication.
No dedicated source was inspected for the canonical Old Deir al-Ghusun record.
A passing agricultural reference is not heritage evidence.
Block Mamluk/Ottoman period labels.
No reliable site-specific source for Khirbet Burj al-Abd near Anabta was inspected.
Block Crusader/Mamluk labels and tower-function narrative.
No dedicated archaeological record for the canonical Khirbet Jaba in Tulkarm was inspected.
The place-name is not unique and creates cross-locality confusion risk.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Tulkarm contains officially recognized built heritage assets, including a museum in a 1908 Ottoman-era building and rehabilitated heritage facilities.

corrections: The canonical record 'Historic Tulkarm City' lacks a verified historic-core boundary.
Roman and Islamic period labels are not supported by the inspected sources.
Create an asset inventory before treating the city as a historic urban property.
No authoritative or academic site record for Maqam Sheikh Shaltout in Tulkarm was located.
Block Ottoman attribution and map use.
The official Qalqilya historic-villages portal does not identify Khirbet Azzun as this specific record.
Block Byzantine/Mamluk labels until a dedicated survey is linked.
No official or academic record for a monument called 'Khirbet Old Qalqilya' was identified.
The label may conflate the city's historic core, nearby ruins, or reused archaeological material.
Block Roman/Mamluk period labels.
No dedicated inspected source for Maqam Nabi Yamin near Azzun was located.
Potential Islamic, Jewish, and biblical name associations require an attributed conflict registry.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Deir Istiya is a recognized Palestinian historic centre with approximately three-century-old buildings, narrow streets, palaces, springs, caves, and ruins.

corrections: The canonical title 'Khirbet Deir Istiya' misclassifies a living historic town/cluster as a single ruin.
Roman and Byzantine period labels require archaeological evidence.
Create constituent records for palaces, shrines, springs, caves, and ruins.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The official Deir Istiya record confirms numerous water springs and the nearby perennial Wadi Qana setting.

corrections: The canonical record 'Historic Water Springs' lacks a constituent list and precise locality.
Roman and Ottoman dates are not verified.
Create one record per spring with coordinates, hydrology, rights, and condition.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The official portal documents Ayyubid and Ottoman shrines in Kifl Haris, including inscription-bearing structures.

corrections: The inspected official record does not support a 'Castle of Kifl Haris'.
The canonical Crusader/Mamluk castle identity requires an independent survey.
Do not substitute shrine histories for castle history.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Tell el-Far'ah North has a major excavation and publication corpus associated with the École biblique and nine campaigns led by Roland de Vaux.
Academic synthesis identifies ordered and fortified Early Bronze settlement phases at Tell el-Far'ah North.

corrections: The label 'Canaanite city' is an oversimplification of a multi-period tell.
Identification with biblical Tirzah must remain a scholarly hypothesis unless explicitly attributed.
Direct page-level extraction from excavation volumes remains pending.
No dedicated archaeological source for 'Khirbet Old Tubas' was inspected.
Block Roman and Byzantine period labels.
No dedicated inspected source distinguishes Ein al-Far'ah as a separate Roman-period site from the wider Wadi/Tell al-Far'ah landscape.
Block Roman attribution and map use.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The property contains deposits of human activity dating to about 10,500 BC.
By the 9th–8th millennium BC it was a sizeable permanent settlement with surviving wall, ditch and tower.
Middle Bronze Age remains indicate a large Canaanite city-state.

corrections: draft_pattern=the oldest city in the world | disposition=REMOVE_ABSOLUTE | replacement=Use the UNESCO-supported chronology and avoid the global superlative unless a comparative scholarly source defines and supports it.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The official Palestinian portal documents monastic caves, a sixth-century monastery phase, and restoration in 1892 at Deir Quruntal.

corrections: The forty-day temptation association remains Christian religious tradition.
The canonical Crusader-period label is not supported by the inspected record.
Do not repeat global 'oldest city' language from the portal in this monastery record.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: Ain es-Sultan is the perennial spring adjacent to and included among the attributes of the inscribed Ancient Jericho/Tell es-Sultan property.

held_claims.claim_text: Independent site boundary outside the property

corrections: Model Ain al-Sultan as a component of the Tell al-Sultan property, not an unrelated independent public site.
Replace the generic Canaanite/Roman period pair with evidence appropriate to the spring and its long settlement relationship.
Prevent duplicate map and publication entries.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The official Palestinian record describes one Nabi Musa shrine complex containing a mosque, mausoleum/tomb, courtyard, rooms, and related facilities.

corrections: The 'Tomb of Nabi Musa' record is a component/alias of the Nabi Musa shrine complex, not a second independent site.
Merge or establish a strict parent-child component relation.
The burial attribution remains religious tradition.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The State Party submission dates the complex to 724–743 AD and says it was most likely built by Hisham and later decorated by al-Walid II.
The submission records destruction in the 749 earthquake and excavations from 1935–1948 by the Palestinian Department of Antiquities under Dimitri Baramki with Robert Hamilton.
The site includes a major bath complex and extensive mosaic decoration, including the Tree of Life panel.

corrections: draft_pattern=Hisham definitively built the palace | disposition=QUALIFY | replacement=Use 'most likely built by Hisham bin Abd al-Malik and later decorated by al-Walid II' unless stronger epigraphic publication is inspected.

coordinate_review.note: The published coordinate notation is internally ambiguous; do not normalize automatically without inspecting the nomination map or geodata.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The wider El-Bariyah landscape contains permanent springs, wadis, monasteries, shrines, and long-term human adaptation to desert water resources.

corrections: No dedicated inspected source was found for the specific canonical Wadi Qelt aqueduct.
The record may conflate multiple channels, springs, periods, and repair phases.
Block the Roman-only attribution, route geometry, and direct map use pending a hydraulic-archaeology source.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The official Palestinian portal identifies Nabi Musa as a Mamluk shrine complex associated institutionally with Sultan al-Zahir Baybars.
The State of Palestine's El-Bariyah submission places Maqam an-Nabi Musa within the Islamic sacred and pilgrimage landscape.

corrections: Merge or relate the separate 'Tomb of Nabi Musa' record as a component of this complex.
The Ottoman period and complete expansion chronology need direct inscriptions, waqf records, or architectural studies.
The tomb attribution remains religious tradition.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: UNESCO lists the Great Omari Mosque among the cultural properties in Gaza with verified damage.
The 2026 State of Palestine Tentative List submission identifies it as the central congregational mosque of historic Gaza and describes Mamluk and Ottoman enlargement of a layered monument.

held_claims.claim_text: Exact destruction severity and surviving fabric

corrections: Do not publish 'oldest and largest mosque' or a 1,400-year minaret age as independently verified.
Do not infer a site-by-site engineering damage grade from UNESCO's public damage list.
Store the 2026 coordinates only as a candidate reference point.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: UNESCO lists Tell el-Ajjul among the archaeological sites with verified damage.
Academic and museum records identify Tell el-Ajjul as a separate Bronze Age archaeological site south of modern Gaza City, with excavated Middle and Late Bronze Age material.

held_claims.claim_text: Exact urban identification with ancient Gaza
Current damage severity and site boundary

corrections: The canonical name conflates Tell el-Ajjul with the historic centre of Gaza; create separate site identities.
Do not describe Tell el-Ajjul as the present Old City of Gaza.
Do not promote any external coordinate without a traceable archaeological geometry.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: UNESCO lists Hamam As-Samra among Gaza properties with verified damage.
A Palestinian cultural-sector report hosted by UNESCO reported complete destruction on 30 December 2023 and described the bath as Gaza's last surviving historic hammam.

corrections: The claimed thousand-year age and Samaritan foundation require direct architectural and archival corroboration.
Do not publish 'completely destroyed' as a current 2026 engineering conclusion without the on-site UNESCO record.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: UNESCO lists Qal'at Barqouq in Khan Younis among properties with verified damage.
The hosted Palestinian report attributes the castle to 1387 in the reign of Sultan Barquq and describes a caravan-route function and surviving façade.

corrections: The 1387 date and functional description require inscription, waqf, or architectural publication corroboration.
Separate the castle from the broader 'Old Khan Younis' cluster.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: UNESCO lists the Saint Porphyrios Orthodox Church Complex among the Gaza properties with verified damage.

The 2026 State Party submission describes an early fifth-century church that remains an active sanctuary, while the Jerusalem Patriarchate confirms the living ecclesiastical identity of the Gaza monastery.

held_claims.claim_text: Exact damage severity and casualty history

corrections: Do not publish global superlatives such as 'third oldest church in the world'.
Separate ecclesiastical tradition from archaeological dating.
Store the Tentative List coordinate only as a blocked external candidate.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: The State of Palestine submitted the Historic Centre of Gaza to UNESCO's Tentative List on 13 January 2026, defining a 1.7 km² historic core with four traditional quarters.
UNESCO's March 2026 assessment verifies damage to a large number of named religious, archaeological, civic, and residential heritage properties within Gaza Governorate.

held_claims.claim_text: Current integrity of the 1.7 km² property

corrections: Treat Historic Gaza as a governed urban cluster, not a single point monument.
Create constituent relationships for the Omari Mosque, Saint Porphyrios, Hamam As-Samra, markets, houses, and other elements.
Tentative List status is not World Heritage inscription or independent verification of every historical assertion.
No dedicated authoritative or academic source for Maqam Sheikh Radwan was located in this wave.
Do not confuse the shrine with the Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood or the Roman cemetery listed there.
Keep chronology, saint attribution, location, and damage status blocked.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: UNESCO lists Anthedon Harbour among the Gaza sites with verified damage.
The State Party Tentative List describes Anthedon as an ancient seaport in northwest Gaza with multi-period remains and explicitly notes uncertainty in precise site identification.

corrections: Do not equate Anthedon automatically with Maiumas or every use of 'old port of Gaza'.
Rename or annotate the canonical Arabic title to preserve the Anthedon/Maiumas distinction.
No direct map coordinate is approved.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: UNESCO verifies damage to Qal'at Barqouq in Khan Younis Governorate.
A Palestinian report hosted by UNESCO records damage to historic houses in Khan Younis and describes Qal'at Barqouq as a principal historic component.

held_claims.claim_text: Current integrity of Khan Younis historic core

corrections: The broader identity 'Old Khan Younis' is not verified as a bounded historic urban property in this wave.
Create a constituent inventory beginning with Qal'at Barqouq instead of treating the cluster as a single monument.

confirmed_claims.claim_text: UNESCO verifies damage to Tell Rafah in Rafah Governorate.

held_claims.claim_text: Exact Tell Rafah chronology and boundary
Current damage severity beyond UNESCO's verification

corrections: The canonical record 'Historic Rafah' is broader than the UNESCO-listed Tell Rafah.
Split the archaeological tell from the modern/historic urban narrative before publication.
No historical chronology or coordinate is promoted in this wave.
